title: SF3352 (2023-2024 Regular): Prohibiting the sale or transfer of a semiautomatic military-style assault weapons, authorizing a buyback program for these weapons and appropriating money

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Minnesota) (gun-policy Stage 5, Minnesota); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Minnesota text (Introduction, 2023-05-19; official copy, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/bills/93/2023/0/SF/3352/versions/0/)
provenance.note: Version read: as-filed (introduced) text; no passage vote recorded. Section 1 strikes the sporting-purposes exclusion from the assault-weapon definition. Section 3 subd. 2 appropriates blank amounts for fiscal years 2024 and 2025 (amounts left as dots); not quoted. Section 2 is effective August 1, 2023, for crimes on or after that date.

operative_text:
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.7145, subd. 2): It is unlawful for a person to transfer a semiautomatic military-style assault weapon.
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.7145, subd. 4): A person who violates subdivision 2 is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $25,000, or both.
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 624.712, subd. 7): (b) Semiautomatic military-style assault weapon also includes any: (1) semiautomatic rifle that has the capacity to accept a detachable magazine and has one or more of the following: (i) a pistol grip or thumbhole stock; (ii) any feature capable of functioning as a protruding grip that can be held by the nontrigger hand; (iii) a folding or telescoping stock; or (iv) a shroud attached to the barrel, or that partially or completely encircles the barrel, allowing the bearer to hold the firearm with the nontrigger hand without being burned, but excluding a slide that encloses the barrel;
Section 3 (uncodified, subd. 1): The commissioner of public safety shall establish a statewide buyback program to purchase semiautomatic military-style assault weapons. The program must accept any semiautomatic military-style assault weapon offered, regardless of the weapon's physical condition, and pay reimbursement at a rate set by the commissioner.
